title: Grade 12 Mathematics — Integrals & Applications of Integrals
description: Integrals and Applications of Integrals practice questions
subject: mathematics

questions.question: ∫xⁿ dx =
questions.explanation: ∫xⁿ dx = xⁿ⁺¹/(n+1) + C for n ≠ −1. This is the power rule of integration (reverse of the differentiation power rule).

questions.question: ∫cos x dx =
questions.explanation: ∫cos x dx = sin x + C. Since d/dx(sin x) = cos x, the integral reverses this.

questions.question: ∫eˣ dx =
questions.explanation: ∫eˣ dx = eˣ + C. The exponential function eˣ is its own derivative and its own integral.

questions.question: The definite integral ∫₀¹ x² dx evaluates to:
The method of integration by substitution uses the substitution u = g(x) to convert:
options: Product of two functions into a simpler form
questions.explanation: In substitution: u = g(x), du = g'(x)dx. So ∫f(g(x))g'(x)dx = ∫f(u)du, which may be easier to evaluate.

questions.question: The formula for integration by parts is:
questions.explanation: Integration by parts (ILATE rule): ∫uv dx = u∫v dx − ∫[(du/dx)(∫v dx)]dx. Choose u using ILATE: Inverse trig, Logarithm, Algebraic, Trigonometric, Exponential.

questions.question: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus states that if F'(x) = f(x), then ∫ₐᵇ f(x) dx =
questions.explanation: Fundamental Theorem of Calculus: ∫ₐᵇ f(x) dx = F(b) − F(a), where F is an antiderivative of f. This connects differentiation and integration.

questions.question: The area under the curve y = f(x) between x = a and x = b is given by:
questions.explanation: Area = ∫ₐᵇ f(x) dx (for f(x) ≥ 0 on [a, b]). The definite integral gives the signed area between the curve and the x-axis.

questions.question: The area of the region bounded by y = x², x = 0, x = 2, and the x-axis is:
The area between two curves y = f(x) and y = g(x) (with f(x) ≥ g(x)) from a to b is:
questions.explanation: Area between two curves = ∫ₐᵇ [upper − lower] dx = ∫ₐᵇ [f(x) − g(x)] dx when f(x) ≥ g(x) on [a, b].

questions.question: The area of the circle x² + y² = r² using integration is:
questions.explanation: By integrating the upper half y = √(r²−x²) from −r to r and doubling: Area = 4∫₀ʳ √(r²−x²) dx = πr².

questions.question: ∫(1/x)dx =
questions.explanation: ∫(1/x)dx = ln|x| + C. This is the special case of the power rule that doesn't apply for n = −1.

questions.question: The area enclosed by the ellipse x²/a² + y²/b² = 1 is:
questions.explanation: The area of an ellipse with semi-major axis a and semi-minor axis b is πab. When a = b = r, this gives πr² (area of a circle).
